dish: clay-oven chicken tandoori and steamed Himalayan momo dumplings
w: Owner Dharma Gurung, a Bhutanese refugee who spent 20 years in Nepal before reaching Erie in 2011, feeds the community authentically flavorful tandoori and Nepali food at affordable prices; she was an Erie Reader '40 Under 40' honoree and the restaurant got its own WQLN 'Erie Eats' episode.

dish: pho tai (rare-beef rice-noodle soup) and banh mi
w: Co-owner Nga Rastatter grew up cooking in her family's restaurant in Vietnam and opened Erie's flagship Vietnamese room in the former Khao Thai building in late 2022 because the nearest pho had been in Cleveland or Pittsburgh; the pho is widely called the best in the city.

dish: kabuli pulao (spiced rice with lamb, carrots and raisins)
w: Erie's first Afghan restaurant, opened February 2025 by Karim Hanif, a physician in Afghanistan before he fled the Taliban; the halal kitchen serves Afghan, Middle Eastern and South Asian dishes and even built a carpeted floor-seating stage so families can eat in the traditional way.

dish: pad thai made to order by the chef-owner
w: Chef Mike Augustine ran a pop-up for nearly a decade before a successful Kickstarter let him settle Like My Thai downtown in early 2015; he cooks every dish himself from an open kitchen in the middle of the room and it is regularly called one of the best restaurants in Erie County.

dish: al pastor and birria tacos with aguas frescas
address: 5630 Peach St Unit A7, Erie, PA 16509
w: A Millcreek taqueria cooking Mexican street food from the owners' home of Guanajuato; Keystone Newsroom's readers voted it Erie's number-one Mexican, and it anchors the Erie Reader's survey of the city's evolving taco scene with standout al pastor and birria.

dish: made-to-order sushi rolls and hibachi (2025 Best of Erie 'Best Sushi')
w: Chef Jufi Andreas, originally from Indonesia, and his wife Sara run this husband-and-wife room blending Japanese and Southeast Asian cooking (sushi, hibachi, even pho); it won Best Sushi in the Erie Reader's 2025 Best of Erie and was featured on WQLN's 'Erie Eats'.

dish: chicken tikka masala and pork momo, made on site
w: A refugee-owned Indian and Himalayan kitchen on Peach Street turning out made-on-site Nepali and North Indian food; it appears in the Erie Reader's roundup of immigrant-owned businesses and the Erie Arts & Culture refugee-owned business directory.

dish: chicken shawarma with garlic sauce, plus falafel and hummus
w: A refugee-owned halal Middle Eastern spot whose shawarma is emblematic of the dish's spread across Erie's international table; listed among the city's immigrant-owned businesses by the Erie Reader and the Erie Arts & Culture refugee directory.

dish: mixed-grill kabobs and chicken mandi, all halal
w: A refugee-owned halal kitchen that moved from French Street to a bigger downtown home on State Street (grand opening covered by YourErie), letting it expand a menu of kabobs, mandi and biryani; also featured in the Erie Reader's immigrant-business coverage.

dish: tacos on house-pressed corn tortillas from an in-house tortilleria
w: Southeast-Mexico cooking built on tortillas pressed in-house; after a 2024 fire shuttered the West 18th Street location, Enrique's reopened inside the downtown Flagship City Food Hall. Featured on WQLN's 'Erie Eats' and in the Erie Reader's taco-scene survey.

A refugee-owned Indian restaurant on Erie's east side rounding out the city's growing South Asian table; documented in the Erie Reader's immigrant-owned business feature and the Erie Arts & Culture refugee-owned business directory.

dish: chicken curry and Indo-Chinese chili chicken
w: Owner Krishna Paudel opened this Indian, Indo-Chinese and Nepali kitchen in the PennWest Edinboro college town in 2024, with a second location planned in Millcreek; the chef brought 15 years of Indian-Nepali cooking from New York and Vermont.
